title: Dağların Efendileri: Doğu Karadeniz Hayvancılık ve Çobanlık Kültürü
summary: Following the emergence of folklore as an academic discipline in Turkey, intensive collection efforts were undertaken to gather material for this field. These efforts, which began during the final years of the Ottoman Empire, continued in a systematic manner during the Republican era; as a result, numerous works representing the oral culture of Anatolian Turks were documented. Starting in the 1960s, collection activities were largely carried out by scholars working at institutional centers (universities, institutes, etc.). During this process, studies were also conducted on the cultural heritage of the Eastern Black Sea Region, a significant area representing Turkish oral culture. We, too, have conducted extensive collection and research activities in this region, which forms the northern border of the Anatolian Turkish cultural geography. This work in your hands was compiled through the presentation and evaluation of materials we identified during 150 days of field research conducted at intervals in the sample areas we had previously determined. Using folklore field research methods such as interviews, participant observation, and case study methods, we have created a very extensive oral and visual archive with the materials we identified. We hope that this archive will provide data for folklore, anthropology, and sociology-related research on local shepherds and livestock herders.
